lessons.title: Inlet, Outlet, and Work Rates
lessons.concept: Pipes and cistern problems are similar to time and work. An inlet pipe fills part of a tank per unit time (positive rate), while an outlet/leak empties part of it (negative rate). If a pipe fills a tank in t hours, its rate is 1/t tank per hour.
lessons.formula: Rate = 1 / time (tank per unit time). Net rate = sum of inlet rates - sum of outlet rates. Time = 1 / net rate.
lessons.worked_example: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and Pipe B fills it in 15 hours. Together in 1 hour they fill 1/10 + 1/15 = (3+2)/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 of the tank. So they fill the tank in 6 hours.
mistakes: Adding times instead of adding rates
Treating an outlet pipe as positive rate
Inverting the final step (rate vs time)

lessons.title: Combined Pipes and Leaks
lessons.concept: When filling and emptying pipes operate together, net effect depends on whether filling rate exceeds emptying rate. If net rate is positive, tank fills; if negative, tank empties. Partial filling and alternating operation should be computed step by step over time intervals.
lessons.formula: Net rate = (1/t1 + 1/t2 + ...) - (1/x1 + 1/x2 + ...). For partial time: work done = net rate * time.
lessons.worked_example: An inlet fills a tank in 8 hours and an outlet empties it in 12 hours. Net rate = 1/8 - 1/12 = (3-2)/24 = 1/24 tank/hour. So the tank fills in 24 hours when both are open.
mistakes: Subtracting times instead of subtracting rates
Assuming tank fills when emptying rate is higher

lessons.title: Sequential and Partial Filling
lessons.concept: Some problems open/close pipes at different times. Compute the fraction filled (or emptied) in each phase and add/subtract contributions. If a pipe is opened for part of the time, only that interval contributes at its rate.
lessons.formula: Total filled = rate1*time1 + rate2*time2 + ...; remaining = 1 - filled (for a full tank).
lessons.worked_example: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours. It is opened alone for 3 hours, then Pipe B (which can fill the tank in 12 hours) is also opened. In 3 hours A fills 3/12 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. Combined rate of A+B = 1/12 + 1/12 = 1/6 per hour. Time to fill remaining = (3/4)/(1/6) = 4.5 hours. Total = 7.5 hours.
mistakes: Applying combined rate to the full duration when pipes were not open together throughout
Forgetting to compute remaining work after first phase
Mixing up fraction of tank with hours

practice.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leak, it takes 8 hours to fill the tank. In how many hours can the leak empty the full tank?
practice.explanation: Inlet rate = 1/6, net rate with leak = 1/8. Leak rate = 1/6 - 1/8 = (4-3)/24 = 1/24 tank/hour. So leak empties full tank in 24 hours.

practice.question: An inlet pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and an outlet pipe empties it in 15 hours. If both are opened together, the tank will be filled in:
practice.explanation: Net rate = 1/10 - 1/15 = (3-2)/30 = 1/30 tank/hour. Time to fill = 30 hours.

practice.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 18 hours. If both are opened for 4 hours, what fraction of the tank is filled?
practice.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = (3+2)/36 = 5/36 tank/hour. In 4 hours, filled = 4 * 5/36 = 20/36 = 5/9.

practice.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 hours and 20 hours respectively. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill half the tank?
practice.explanation: Combined rate = 1/15 + 1/20 = (4+3)/60 = 7/60 tank/hour. Time for full tank = 60/7 hours. Time for half tank = (1/2)/(7/60) = 30/7 = 4 2/7 hours.

questions.question: A tap can fill a cistern in 8 hours. After half the cistern is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the cistern completely?
questions.explanation: One tap fills in 8 hours, so half cistern takes 4 hours. Remaining half is filled by 4 similar taps. Rate of 4 taps = 4/8 = 1/2 cistern/hour. Time for remaining half = (1/2)/(1/2) = 1 hour. Total time = 4 + 1 = 5 hours.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 9 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it is filled in 10 hours. If the tank is full, in how much time will the leak empty it?
questions.explanation: Fill rate = 1/9, net rate = 1/10. Leak rate = 1/9 - 1/10 = (10-9)/90 = 1/90 tank/hour. So leak empties full tank in 90 hours.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. If A is opened first and after 5 minutes B is also opened, in how many more minutes will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: In 5 minutes, A fills 5/20 = 1/4 of tank. Remaining = 3/4. Combined rate of A and B = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3+2)/60 = 1/12 tank/minute. Time for remaining = (3/4)/(1/12) = 9 minutes.
